paper.title: Selecting the best system and multi-armed bandits

settings.name_in_paper: P(epsilon,delta) / P_a(epsilon) policies on KL right dense collection L (lower bound)
unmapped: Distribution class is KL right dense (finite means, unbounded support on the right; e.g. all light-tailed distributions with unbounded right support)
Indifference-zone guarantee: correctness required only when best mean exceeds second-best by known epsilon
settings.definition_quote:
A collection of probability distributions ${\cal L}$  is referred to as $KL$ right dense, if each distribution has finite mean and  if for every $G\in {\cal L}$,
and every $\alpha>0$, $\beta> \mu_G$,  there exists a distribution  $G_{\beta} \in {\cal L}$
such that (\ref{eqn:neg_result_odd_space1}) and (\ref{eqn:neg_result_odd_space2}) hold.

settings.name_in_paper: Selecting the best population among non-negative random variables with known moment bounds E f_i(X(i)) <= c_i
unmapped: Non-negative rewards with known bounds E f_i(X(i)) <= c_i for known strictly convex non-decreasing f_i; learner knows f_i and c_i
Indifference zone: best mean exceeds others by known epsilon
settings.definition_quote: let Y denote a collection probability distributions corresponding to non-negative random variables (X(i): i <= d) such that there exists strictly convex, non-decreasing functions (f_i(.): i <= d) and positive constants (c_i: i <= d) so that E f_i(X(i)) <= c_i for all i.
